question: Which three temperature zones have their own selector on the A320 AIR COND panel?

options.text: Left cabin, right cabin and cockpit
Cockpit, forward cabin and aft cabin

explanation: The panel carries COCKPIT, FWD CABIN and AFT CABIN selectors. Cargo has its own ventilation and is not one of the three conditioned zones.

question: What temperature does a zone selector request in its 12 o'clock position?
explanation: The mid position is about 24 °C. The scale runs from about 18 °C at COLD to about 30 °C at HOT.

question: What temperature does a zone selector request at the COLD stop?
explanation: COLD is about 18 °C. The selectors cover roughly 18–30 °C, with 24 °C at the top.

question: What temperature does a zone selector request at the HOT stop?
explanation: HOT is about 30 °C. The selectors cover roughly 18–30 °C, with 24 °C at the top.

question: How do PACK 1 and PACK 2 operate in normal use?

options.text: Pack 2 follows pack 1 as a slave
Automatically and independently of each other
Only one runs at a time and they alternate each flight
Manually, from the PACK FLOW selector

explanation: Each pack has its own controller and flow control valve; the loss of one does not take the other with it.

question: What does the PACK pushbutton in the ON (lights out) position do?

options.text: It opens the pack flow control valve fully regardless of demand
It selects HI flow on that pack
It opens the ram air inlet of that pack
The pack flow control valve is automatically controlled

explanation: ON hands the valve to automatic control. The valve still closes automatically for its protections.

question: What happens when a PACK pushbutton is selected OFF?

options.text: The pack flow control valve closes
The pack keeps running but its trim air stops
The pack goes to LO flow

explanation: Selecting OFF shuts the pack's flow control valve, so that pack delivers no air.

question: Which condition does NOT turn on the amber PACK FAULT light?

options.text: The pack flow control valve disagreeing with the selected position
The PACK FLOW selector set to LO

explanation: FAULT means a valve disagreement or a pack overheat (compressor outlet or pack outlet). Flow selection is a normal setting, not a fault.

question: What flow does the PACK FLOW selector give in LO?
explanation: LO is 80 %, NORM 100 % and HI 120 %.

question: What flow does the PACK FLOW selector give in HI?
explanation: HI is 120 %, used for smoke removal and hot or wet conditions.

question: In which situation is the PACK FLOW selector setting irrelevant, the flow being HI regardless?

options.text: Whenever the aircraft is on the ground with engines running
Single pack operation, or when the APU bleed is supplying the packs
Whenever the zone selectors are at COLD

explanation: With only one pack, or with APU bleed air, the system always uses HI flow; the selector has no effect.

question: LO pack flow is selected, but the cooling demand cannot be met. What does the system do?

options.text: It goes to 100 % flow even though LO is selected
It stays at 80 % and the zones warm up
It shuts the trim air valves

explanation: LO is a request, not a limit: if cooling cannot be satisfied the flow rises to NORM.

question: On what basis is the PACK FLOW selector set?

options.text: The number of passengers and the ambient conditions (smoke removal, hot or wet conditions)

explanation: Fewer passengers allow LO to save bleed air; smoke removal and hot or humid days call for HI.

question: What does the HOT AIR pushbutton in the ON position provide?

options.text: Hot air to the wing anti-ice
Hot air to the cargo heating only
Hot air for the trim air system
Hot air to the packs' anti-ice valves

explanation: HOT AIR ON opens the hot air pressure regulating valve so trim air is available to raise each zone's temperature.

question: What happens when the HOT AIR pushbutton is selected OFF?

options.text: The hot air valve closes and any FAULT is reset
The trim air valves open fully
The zone controller switches to its secondary channel

explanation: OFF closes the hot air valve; it is also the action that clears a HOT AIR FAULT.

question: At what duct temperature does the HOT AIR FAULT light come on?
explanation: A duct overheat above 88 °C gives the amber FAULT and an ECAM caution, and the valves close automatically.

question: After a HOT AIR FAULT, when does the FAULT light go out by itself?

options.text: When the duct temperature falls below 70 °C (158 °F)
Only when the zone selectors are turned to COLD

explanation: The light goes out below 70 °C, or when the crew selects the pushbutton OFF.

question: What does pressing the guarded RAM AIR pushbutton ON do?

options.text: It opens the emergency ram air inlet
It opens the pack ram air inlet flaps fully
It switches the packs to HI flow

explanation: RAM AIR is a separate emergency inlet, used to ventilate the aircraft when the packs are lost or for smoke removal.

question: RAM AIR is selected ON while the cabin differential pressure is 1 psi or more. What happens?

options.text: Ram air flows in and the cabin depressurises
The outflow valve control stays normal and no emergency ram air flows in

explanation: Ram air pressure cannot overcome a cabin at 1 psi or more above ambient, so nothing flows until the differential falls.

question: RAM AIR is ON, differential pressure is below 1 psi and pressurisation is in automatic. What does the outflow valve do?
explanation: Opening the outflow valve about halfway gives the incoming ram air a way out, so it flows through the cabin.

question: RAM AIR is ON with pressurisation in manual mode. What does the outflow valve do automatically?

options.text: Nothing: it does not open automatically under manual control

explanation: In MAN the crew drives the outflow valve with MAN V/S CTL; the automatic opening only happens under automatic control.

question: Where does emergency ram air go once it flows in?
explanation: Emergency ram air bypasses the packs and enters the mixer unit, from where it is distributed to the zones.

question: What does DITCHING do to the emergency ram air inlet?

options.text: It closes it, even if RAM AIR is ON
It opens it to flood the cabin slowly
It has no effect on it
It opens it to equalise pressure

explanation: Ditching closes every opening below the floating line, the ram air inlet included.

question: What does a green ALTN MODE message on the ECAM COND page mean?

options.text: Both packs are in alternate flow
The primary zone controller is faulty

explanation: ALTN MODE shows that the zone controller's primary channel has failed and its back-up is in use.

question: What does a green PACK REG message on the ECAM COND page mean?

options.text: The packs are operating in HI flow
The pack flow control valves are closed
The zone controller is faulty, so the packs regulate the temperature themselves

explanation: With the zone controller lost, the pack controllers take over temperature regulation on their own.

question: What does an amber FAN on the ECAM COND page indicate?

options.text: The avionics blower fan is faulty
The cargo extraction fan has stopped
The lavatory extraction fan is off

explanation: The FAN indication on the COND page concerns the cabin recirculation fans.

question: Above what duct temperature does a zone's duct temperature turn amber on the COND page?
explanation: The duct indication turns amber above 80 °C — an early sign of trim air heating too much.

question: On the COND page, the hot air pressure regulating valve shows an amber crossline. What does that mean?

options.text: HOT AIR is OFF with the valve closed, or the valve disagrees with its commanded position
The valve is open and operating normally
The hot air duct is leaking
The trim air valves are fully open

explanation: A green crossline is a normally closed valve with the button in AUTO; amber flags OFF or a disagreement.

question: Above what temperature does the pack outlet temperature turn amber on the BLEED page?
explanation: Pack outlet above 90 °C is an overheat indication.

question: Above what temperature does the pack compressor outlet temperature turn amber on the BLEED page?
explanation: The compressor outlet is the hottest point inside the pack; amber above 230 °C indicates an overheat.

question: On the BLEED page, how is a pack ram air inlet flap that is fully open on the ground shown?

options.text: It is not shown on the ground

explanation: Fully open in flight is green; fully open on the ground is amber.

question: What do the letters C and H next to a pack's turbine bypass valve on the BLEED page mean?

options.text: C: cross bleed closed; H: HP valve open
C: controller channel; H: heating mode
C: the valve is closed (cold); H: the valve is open (hot)

explanation: The bypass valve sends hot air around the cooling turbine. Closed gives the coldest outlet, open the hottest.

question: When is the pack flow indication shown in amber on the BLEED page?

options.text: When the ram air flap is open
When the pack flow control valve is closed
When the APU supplies the pack

explanation: Amber pack flow means no flow through that pack because its flow control valve is closed.
